blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A year after Typhoon Tino’s deadly floods exposed Cebu’s vulnerability to extreme rainfall, provincial and city officials are pursuing stronger flood mitigation, early warning systems and disaster response measures to reduce the risks to communities. Cebu Gov. Pamela Baricuatro is prioritizing long-term flood control interventions, including proposed dams along four major river systems, while Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival is looking to improve rescue capabilities, equipment and coordination with neighboring local governments. Their efforts reflect lessons from Tino, which killed 143 people, injured 5,079 and left 45 missing across Cebu province, according to Provincial Government records as […]...
